---
title: "Using skd from Python"
execute:
  eval: false
---

spice-kernel-db manages kernel files; it loads nothing. From Python you fetch,
index and check metakernels with it, then hand the resulting path to spiceypy.
This page walks through that from a fresh install to a light-time computation.
The code is not executed when the docs build, because every step talks to
NAIF or to your own store; run it in a notebook or a script.

The names used here are the public API, `spice_kernel_db.__all__`, listed on
the [home page](index.qmd#public-api) and documented in the
[reference](../reference/index.html). They are kept stable within a major
version, so a project can pin `spice-kernel-db>=0.30,<1`.

## Two ways in

**One call against the configured database.** The module-level functions open
the database named in your config, do one thing and close it:

```python
from spice_kernel_db import check, get, metakernels_covering, resolve_metakernel, scan

get("https://naif.jpl.nasa.gov/pub/naif/JUICE/kernels/mk/juice_ops.tm", yes=True)
report = check("juice_ops")
path = resolve_metakernel("juice_ops")
```

**A `KernelDB` for several operations.** It is a context manager, and a
`console=` makes it print what the CLI prints:

```python
from rich.console import Console
from spice_kernel_db import KernelDB

with KernelDB(console=Console()) as db:
    db.list_metakernels()
    db.check_report("juice_ops")
```

Without a console (the default) nothing is printed, progress bars are off, and
every question is answered no, so a script passes `yes=True` where it wants a
download. Warnings go through the `spice_kernel_db` logger; configure
`logging` to see them.

## Fetch a metakernel

`get` takes a URL the first time and a tracked name after that:

```python
from spice_kernel_db import get

result = get(
    "https://naif.jpl.nasa.gov/pub/naif/JUICE/kernels/mk/juice_ops.tm",
    mission="JUICE",
    yes=True,
)
result["downloaded"]   # the kernel files written
result["warnings"]     # anything the downloader could not fetch
```

Where the files land is derived: the kernel root that already holds the
metakernel or its mission, else the only configured root. With several roots
and no such fact `AmbiguousKernelRoot` is raised; `download_dir=` is the
explicit answer. The `.tm` skd writes carries absolute `PATH_VALUES`, so it
works from any working directory.

Re-fetching later needs only the name, and `yes=True` once more:

```python
get("juice_ops", yes=True)
```

## Check it

```python
from spice_kernel_db import check

report = check("juice_ops")
report["exit_code"]      # 0 when every kernel is present and every entry resolves
for verdict in report["verdicts"]:
    print(verdict["ok"], verdict["line"])   # ok is True, False or None (not checked)
```

`exit_code` is a sum of bits: 1 a kernel is missing, 2 an entry does not
resolve, 4 a kernel differs from the server (only with `remote=True`). A
script can branch on it the way `skd check` lets a shell script branch.

## Hand it to spiceypy

```python
import spiceypy as spice
from spice_kernel_db import resolve_metakernel

spice.furnsh(str(resolve_metakernel("juice_ops")))
```

`resolve_metakernel` accepts any form a user might have in hand: the registry
filename, the version-stripped base name, a path, or the source URL. An
untracked name raises `MetakernelNotTracked`; a name matching several tracked
metakernels raises `AmbiguousMetakernel` with the candidates.

## Which metakernel covers a body at a time?

```python
import spiceypy as spice
from spice_kernel_db import metakernels_covering

et = spice.utc2et("2032-01-15T00:00:00")
rows = metakernels_covering(body_id=-28, et=et)   # JUICE
rows[0]["filename"], rows[0]["intervals"]
```

This reads the SPK coverage of every tracked metakernel's kernels and needs
spiceypy (the `[spice]` extra).

## Kernels you already have

```python
from spice_kernel_db import register_metakernel, scan

scan("/data/spice/MRO/kernels", mission="MRO")          # index kernel files
register_metakernel("/data/spice/mk/mro_2024.tm", mission="MRO", official=False)
```

`official=False` marks a metakernel assembled locally, such as the output of
NAIF's subsetter, so `ls` and `show` say so.

## A complete example

```python
import logging

import spiceypy as spice
from spice_kernel_db import check, get, resolve_metakernel

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING)   # see skd's warnings

get("https://naif.jpl.nasa.gov/pub/naif/JUICE/kernels/mk/juice_ops.tm", yes=True)
if check("juice_ops")["exit_code"]:
    raise SystemExit("juice_ops is incomplete; run `skd check juice_ops` for the detail")

spice.furnsh(str(resolve_metakernel("juice_ops")))
et = spice.utc2et("2032-01-15T00:00:00")
_, light_time = spice.spkpos("JUICE", et, "J2000", "NONE", "EARTH")
print(f"one-way light time Earth to JUICE: {light_time / 60:.1f} min")
```

## Errors you can catch

| Exception | Raised when | CLI exit code |
|:---|:---|---|
| `MetakernelNotTracked` | a name matches nothing skd tracks | 1 |
| `AmbiguousMetakernel` | a name matches several tracked metakernels | 2 |
| `AmbiguousKernelRoot` | several roots and nothing says which holds a download | 2 |
| `MetakernelUnreachableError` | the source of a tracked metakernel is gone (HTTP 403, 404, 410) | 2 |
| `ConcurrentModificationError` | another process changed the records during a download | 1 |
| `ConfigError` | the config file does not parse, or none exists and nothing seeds it | 78 |

All are importable from `spice_kernel_db`.

## Hosting the command line

A program with its own Typer CLI can mount skd's command tree as one of its
groups; planetarypy does this as `plp spice`:

```python
import typer
from spice_kernel_db.cli import app as skd_app, exit_code, logging_to_stderr

app = typer.Typer()
app.add_typer(skd_app, name="spice")


def main() -> None:
    try:
        with logging_to_stderr():
            app()
    except Exception as exc:
        code = exit_code(exc)   # None for anything that is not skd's
        if code is None:
            raise
        typer.echo(str(exc), err=True)
        raise SystemExit(code)
```

`app`, `exit_code` and `logging_to_stderr` are the host contract and change
only with a major version.
